picked.t: 韓컨소시엄, 5,600억 ‘베트남 북남고속철’ 설계용역 따내…해외철도 설계 역대 최대 수주성과
picked.body: 베트남 북남고속철도 노선도. (이미지=국토교통부) 국가철도공단 등 한국 기업이 참여한 컨소시엄이 베트남 북남고속철도 사업의 타당성조사(F/S)·기본설계(FEED) 용역(TV02 패키지)을 수주했다. 국토교통부는 “국가철도공단과 삼보, 유신 등 국내 기업이 참여한 컨소시엄이 지난 21일 베트남 북남고속철도 설계용역을 수주했다”며 “이번 사업은 해외 철도 계획·설계 분야에서 한국 기업이 참여해 거둔 수주 가운데 역대 최대 규모”라고 22일 밝혔다. 국토부에 따르면 컨소시엄에는 국가철도공단과 종합 엔지니어링 컨설팅 업체 삼보와 유신 등 우리 기업과 프랑스 시스트라(SYSTRA), 베트남 교통운송설계자문총공사(TEDI) 등 3개국 기업이 포함됐다. 발주처인 베트남 건설부 산하 탕롱(Thang Long) 사업관리위원회에 따르면, TV02 패키지는 △타당성조사 보고서 작성 △기본설계(FEED) △건설∙설치 입찰 서류 작성 등과 함께 전체 노선 상 경로를 따라 1만 헥타르(ha) 이상의 면적에 대한 토지 조사 등이 주요 업무로, 단순한 조사를 넘어 프로젝트의 뼈대를 만드는 핵심 컨설팅 용역으로, 사업비는 10조7,820억 동(4억1,840만여 달러, 원화 약 5,640억 원)에 달한다. 앞서 탕롱사업관리위원회는 이달 초 “북남고속철도 TV02 패키지 입찰에서 응찰한 곳은 국내외 기업으로 구성된 컨소시엄 1곳뿐이었다”며 이달 중 입찰 평가 결과를 발표하겠다고 밝힌 바 있다. 그러나 당시 발주처는 응찰 컨소시엄을 국내 기업 4곳, 외국 기업 4곳으로 설명해 이번 국토부 발표와 다소 차이를 보인다. 한편, 국토부에 따르면, 이번 컨소시엄의 용역 기간은 30개월로 이달부터 2029년 5월까지 타당성조사에 18개월, 기본설계에 12개월이 각각 배정됐다. 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 한국 정부는 이번 수주에 정부 차원의 지원 활동이 뒷받침됐다고 설명했다. 지난해 8월과 올해 4월 한·베트남 정상회담에서 고속철도 협력이 논의됐고, 올해 6월에는 국토부 2차관이 이끈 수주지원단이 베트남을 찾았다. 7월에는 당시 국토부 장관이 방문해 이재명 대통령의 친서를 전달했다. 앞서 베트남 국회가 승인한 계획에 따르면, 북남고속철도는 15개 성·시를 거쳐 하노이와 호치민시를 잇는 총연장 1,541km 노선으로, 총사업비 1,713조5,480억 동(665억 달러)이 투입되는 베트남 역사상 최대 규모의 철도 인프라 사업이다. 본 노선은 설계 속도 시속 350km의 표준궤(1,435mm) 복선철도로 계획됐으며, 전체 구간에는 여객역 23개와 화물역 5개가 들어선다. 북남고속철도는 완공 시, 하노이와 호치민시 간 이동시간이 5시간대로 단축, 국토 전역이 일일 생활권으로 묶이게 돼 베트남 경제 성장을 가속화할 핵심 동력이 될 것으로 기대를 모으고 있다. 완공 목표는 2035년으로, 착공 시점은 준비 상황에 따라 조정되고 있다. 국토부는 이번 용역에서 쌓은 경험과 협력 관계를 토대로 철도 건설과 차량 제작, 운영 등 본사업에도 한국 기업이 참여할 수 있도록 지원하겠다는 방침이다. 한편, 베트남 건설부는 연말까지 TV02 패키지 본계약을 체결할 계획이다.

Held on Sunday at the Van Phuc Diplomatic Compound, the festival featured a culinary showcase of banh mi from Vietnam's northern, central, and southern regions. According to Le Van Khanh (4th L), an artisan and member of the Vietnam Culinary Culture Association, the loaves were baked in different colors to represent each region, white for the north, moringa-infused green for the central region, and beetroot-dyed pink for the south. Among the guests at the event's opening were Ngo Phuong Ly, wife of Vietnam's Party General Secretary and President To Lam, and Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung and his wife. They went around and chatted with the artisans. Once baked, the loaves were filled with typical toppings from their respective regions, including pâté, pork sausage ( gio cha ), grilled meats, mayonnaise, herbs, and sauces before being sliced into bite-sized portions. From a street food staple, banh mi has evolved into an ambassador for Vietnamese cuisine, and the festival highlighted both its regional diversity and the creativity of local artisans. Running from Saturday to Sunday ahead of Vietnam Culture Day (Nov. 24), the festival had nearly 100 booths representing 46 countries and 11 Vietnamese provinces and cities. Organizers expected 25,000 visitors this year, up 25% from last year's 20,000. Photos by Giang Huy

picked.t: Explore Mang Den treehouse village, Vietnam's nominee for global tourism award
picked.body: Mang Den Treehouse Village is on Su Van Hanh Street, near Dak Ke Lake in Mang Den Commune, Quang Ngai Province. Recognized as a tourist attraction in August 2025, it stands out for its accommodation in houses built among the trees of a pine forest. In October, the village was selected as one of five Vietnamese nominees for the "Best Tourism Villages" award from the United Nations Tourism Organization (UN Tourism). The wooden houses are scattered across tree trunks, hidden beneath the canopy. Instead of rows of packed rooms, the houses are placed among the trees and linked by elevated walkways. According to the Vietnam National Authority of Tourism, the design aims to limit its impact on the terrain and vegetation. Rather than cutting down trees to clear space, some structures are built around the trunks, and trees even grow through the houses. Visitors can walk the Skywalk, a system of wooden bridges that pass through the treetops. From there, they can view the forest from above. Those who prefer more outdoor activities can try ziplining through the forest, trekking trails, cycling, or exploring areas with streams and coffee gardens. Beyond the scenery, the village aims to tie tourism to the local community. It prioritizes hiring Ba Na and Xo Dang workers and buys ingredients and handicrafts from farming households and artisans. The resort also hosts cultural exchanges with artisans, including gong performances (a musical instrument native to the Central Highlands) and traditional dance. The resort says it has replaced single-use plastics with materials such as wood, bamboo and glass. It sorts waste at the source, uses organic waste as fertilizer and sends the remainder to a collection and recycling unit. The period from November to April brings drier weather, favorable for outdoor activities in Mang Den. At around 1,200 meters above sea level, the area is cool, with chilly early mornings and nights. Late in the year, visitors may also see wild sunflowers blooming along some roads, depending on the weather each year. Besides staying in the treehouse village, visitors can combine their trip with Dak Ke Lake, Pa Sy Waterfall, Khanh Lam Pagoda or the community villages around Mang Den. The Best Tourism Villages award looks beyond scenery and visitor appeal. It evaluates how well a village protects nature and local culture, supports community jobs and economic growth, and manages tourism sustainably. Vietnam's other four nominees are Lo Village (Dak Lak Province), Cat Cat (Lao Cai Province), Bay Mau coconut forest (Da Nang) and Huu Lien (Lang Son Province). UN Tourism is expected to announce the results in the fourth quarter. Previously, five Vietnamese destinations have received the title: Lo Lo Chai (Tuyen Quang Province), Quynh Son (Lang Son Province), Thai Hai (Thai Nguyen Province), Tan Hoa (Quang Tri Province) and Tra Que (Da Nang ). Photos by Mang Den Treehouse Village

picked.t: 베트남, ‘에어비앤비’ 등 공유숙박업 제도권 편입…개정 주택법
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시에 위치한 한 고급아파트. 베트남이 법 개정을 통해 그동안 제도권 밖에 있던 공유숙박업을 합법화할 법적 기반을 마련했다. 베트남 국회는 이러한 내용을 골자로 한 주택법 개정안을 지난 21일 가결 처리했다. 내년 7월부터 시행되는 개정법은 아파트를 주거 외 용도로 쓰지 못하게 한 금지 규정에 예외 조항을 추가해 그동안 논란이 일었던 에어비앤비 같은 플랫폼을 통한 단기숙박업을 제도권 내로 끌어들일 기반을 마련했다. 자세히 살펴보면, 개정 주택법 제3조는 아파트를 주거 외 목적으로 쓰는 행위를 금지하면서 동시에 주거용 또는 숙박용으로 임대하는 경우는 예외로 뒀다. 제12조에는 소유자의 권리로 기존의 거주, 주거용 임대에 더해 숙박 임대가 추가됐다. 단, 아파트를 주거용이나 숙박용으로 임대하려는 소유자는 공동주택 관리·사용 규정이 정한 보안과 질서 유지 요건을 준수해야 한다. 이는 기존 2023년 주택법과 비교했을 때 상당한 변화다. 앞서 개정 전 주택법은 아파트를 주거용 임대를 제외한 나머지 비주거 용도 사용을 금지하고 있었다. 최근 수년간 베트남을 찾는 외국인이 급증하면서 공유숙박업 시장도 큰 폭의 성장세를 보였지만, 기존 법률 체계에서 숙박 목적의 임대는 예외로 인정되지 않아 아파트를 사업장으로 활용하는 임대사업자들은 많은 어려움을 겪었다. 베트남 대도시를 중심으로 크게 성장한 공유숙박업은 관련 법률 부재 속에 임대인과 입주자 사이 찬반이 극명하게 엇갈리며 논란을 겪었다. 임대인들은 비어 있는 아파트를 활용해 관광객과 출장자 등의 숙박 수요를 채울 수 있고, 이는 자산을 합법적으로 활용할 권리라고 주장했던 반면, 입주민과 관리위원회는 투숙객이 계속 드나들면 보안이 불안해지고 생활 공간이 침해되며, 인프라 시설 부담과 관리·운영 분쟁도 커진다며 맞섰다. 로비에 공유숙박업 금지 X배너가 설치돼 있던 호치민시의 한 아파트.   논란이 이어지자 하노이와 호치민시 등 일부 지방자치단체는 2023년 주택법의 비주거 용도 사용 금지 조항을 근거로 아파트 숙박 임대 단속을 강화해 왔다. 그러나 임대인의 재산권과 입주민의 주거권을 두고 규정을 해석하고 적용하는 방식이 지역마다 달라 갈등이 지속됐다. 한편, 이번 개정법에 대해 업계 전문가들은 “새로운 규정이 에어비앤비 같은 플랫폼 기반 사업 모델의 법적 틀을 마련해 법적 논란이 많던 공유숙박업을 관리 체계 안으로 끌어들이는 효과가 있을 것”이라는 기대감을 나타냈다. 베트남부동산중개인협회(VARS)의 응우옌 찌 탄(Nguyen Chi Thanh) 부회장은 “아파트 소유주의 재산권과 다른 입주민의 안전하고 사생활이 보장되는 주거권 사이의 균형을 위해 관리 당국은 숙박용 아파트의 기준과 투숙객 등록·신고 책임, 소방 요건, 보험, 세금 의무에 대한 통일된 지침을 조속히 발표해야 한다”고 밝혔다.

picked.t: Outlet centers and duty-free shops proposed for Vietnam’s largest airport Long Thanh
picked.body: The Dong Nai People’s Committee’s draft resolution sets out the types of projects that could be developed, along with investment incentives, support policies and procedures. Under the proposal, manufacturers and distributors would sell legally sourced branded goods directly to shoppers at outlet prices. The centers could range from large outlet villages combining shopping with tourism, dining, entertainment and events to smaller urban and suburban sites serving residents and visitors. Some could become part of existing malls and commercial complexes. Priority locations include the airport and its surrounding airport city, the Ho Chi Minh City–Long Thanh–Dau Giay Expressway corridor, planned ring roads, logistics hubs, industrial parks and designated riverside commercial and tourism zones. The draft also proposes duty-free shops and VAT refund outlets at the airport’s international terminal and approved outlet centers. Approved investors would be expected to aim for Vietnamese goods to account for 30–40% of total product value, or for a share suited to each product category. Long Thanh International Airport spans about 5,000 hectares and represents an investment of more than US$16 billion. It is designed to meet the International Civil Aviation Organization’s highest airport classification, 4F. Once all phases are complete, the airport is expected to handle 100 million passengers and five million tonnes of cargo a year, positioning it as a major aviation hub in the Asia-Pacific. Construction is being accelerated, with the first commercial flight scheduled for Dec. 24.

picked.t: Indian mother who opposed son’s marriage to Vietnamese woman finds second home in daughter-in-law’s homeland
picked.body: At 6 a.m., Kamala steps out of the elevator at her apartment complex in Binh Hung Commune, Ho Chi Minh city, and waves to some seniors warming up in the yard. The 61-year-old from India does not speak Vietnamese or English, and so gets by with smiles and nods. She joins the group for 15 minutes of gentle exercise and walks for a while before heading upstairs. It is a change from her life in Tamil Nadu, India, where she raised two sons on her own after her husband died. There, she spent most of her time at home or visiting temples. In 2020, her eldest son, Prakash Singh, moved to Vietnam to work as an IT engineer and met Ngo Thuy Duong, 36, of Mekong Delta ward of Soc Trang. When he told his mother he wanted to marry Duong, Kamala objected. In her family, marriages had always been arranged between people of similar backgrounds, religions, and castes. For six months, Prakash called his mother in India every evening, insistently telling her Duong was the only woman he would marry. Seeing how determined he was, she finally agreed. Before the wedding, Prakash and Duong agreed they would make their home in Vietnam. The couple married in late 2021. Kamala initially planned to stay in India with her younger son, but after he married and moved out, she had to manage on her own in a large house, and it was a hassle. Duong and Prakash then talked about bringing her to Ho Chi Minh City. Kamala had visited Vietnam before, but had turned down the idea of settling there, worried she would have trouble adjusting. But this time, the couple persuaded her to stay with them for a month. Before she arrived, Duong went to Indian grocery stores and stocked the kitchen with stuff like basmati rice, ground turmeric powder, cardamom, dill seeds, and beans. For the first few weeks, Kamala rarely left the apartment. Whenever she opened the door and found olderneighbors gathered in the hallway and asking how she was, she would lower her head, smile, and close the door again as her shyness would take over. Inside, she had a routine: rise early to clean the altar with idols of Hindu deities she had brought from India, light incense, offer fruits, and pray. She would read at midday and cook in the afternoon. The hardest adjustment for Kamala and Duong was in the kitchen since the Indian woman has complicated rules for eating meat. Sometimes she goes three months without eating any meat or seafood. At other times, she eats meat but only on two days of a week, on Wednesdays and Sundays. It is down to Hindu religious reasons. But during her vegetarian bouts, she has to keep all vessels used to make meat, fish, and even eggs away from the vegetarian utensils since they are considered to "defile" the former. These included pots, pans, knives, cutting boards, and even dish sponges. But in their small kitchen, Duong would often store both foods side by side or use the same utensils for both. One day, Kamala saw her do it, went quietly into her room, shut the door, and did not speak to the couple for several days. Prakash then explained to Duong the Hindu rules about ritual purity that his mother followed. He told his mother that Vietnamese families are used to sharing utensils but wash them thoroughly after use. Duong then bought a new set of utensils and labeled them clearly. She sometimes bought her mother-in-law banh da lon (steamed layer cake) or banh chuoi nuong (baked banana cake) for a change. Kamala says both are delicious, but sticks nevertheless to rice and Indian-style sauces and curries. Duong told Prakash to take his mother downstairs for walks so that she could get some exercise. Kamala grew curious about the older residents she saw working out. When they took her by the hand and invited her to join, she went along. Fresh air and such friendly company gradually helped her feel less cooped up. Kamala grew more at ease with her daughter-in-law, too. When Duong cracked a joke or put an arm around her as they cooked, she would stiffen, unsure how to respond. But soon, she relaxed and began reaching for her daughter-in-law’s hand herself. When she visited Duong’s family in Soc Trang, she walked through their fruit orchards. The family would go to the market early and treat her to vegetarian meals of tofu braised with lemongrass and chili and sour vegetable soups. "Vietnamese people make me feel like I’m part of their family," she says. Now, Kamala joins her neighbors regularly for morning exercises. In the afternoon, she helps Duong sort vegetables and plays with her young grandchild. On weekends, Duong and Prakash take her to a Hindu temple. When she misses home, Prakash asks someone he knows to accompany her and help her travel back to India to spend a few weeks with relatives. "My mother smiles more now, sleeps well, and has friends to talk to every morning. Bringing her to live in Vietnam was absolutely the right decision," he says.

picked.t: Six experiences for young travelers at Ba Na Hills this festive season
picked.body: Sun World Ba Na Hills, located nearly 1,500 meters above sea level on Chua Mountain in Da Nang, is introducing a series of cultural and entertainment activities for the 2026 year-end holiday season. The mountain complex features European-inspired architecture, including Moon Castle, the French Village, and Eclipse Square, alongside the Golden Bridge, known for its two giant stone hands. Visitors can explore Fantasy Park, ride the dual-track Alpine Coaster at speeds of up to 40 kph, or watch performances such as "After Glow," "Love in the Sky," and the "Cancan" dance. The Eric Kayser bakery at Ba Na Hills provides a dining stop within the mountain complex's European-inspired setting. Through Dec. 31, visitors aged 18-25 can purchase promotional cable car tickets for VND500,000 (US$19) upon presenting a valid citizen identification card, passport, or verified VNeID account. Other options include an VND800,000 package combining cable car admission with a lunch buffet or an VND750,000 package including admission and a dining voucher. Each promotional cable car ticket also comes with a choice of a complimentary French pastry at Eric Kayser or two 250 ml glasses of Sun Kraftbeer accompanied by a guided tour of Ba Na Brew House. A new Golden Leaf Path at the entrance to Rose Hall in Eclipse Square offers visitors a setting inspired by autumn scenery. The installation features a canopy of orange and red leaves stretching above a walkway covered in artificial foliage, creating a backdrop for photographs. Dream Town, a new Christmas-themed attraction at Ba Na Hills, is scheduled to open on Dec. 1, operating daily from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m. Designed around a Christmas village concept, the attraction will feature Santa Claus's house, festive decorations, and interactive entertainment. Visitors will be able to write letters to Santa Claus, take part in photo activities, receive surprise gifts, and watch performances featuring Santa and Mrs. Claus characters. The "Origin" Interactive Light Art Space, located near Louvre Station at Ba Na Hills, covers nearly 800 square meters and features seven interactive zones. Using light sensors and digital technology, the installation responds to visitors' movements and touch, creating changing visual effects. Other indoor attractions include the 4D "Lunar Intersection" cinema and the VR Airship "Flying Eyes" experience inside Moon Castle, both of which are available without additional admission charges, according to the operator. Ba Na Hills is also hosting Chu Choa Market in the Hoi An-Truong Lang area to celebrate Vietnam Culture Day on Nov. 24. Inspired by the culture of Quang Nam, the market recreates a traditional countryside setting with bamboo decorations, woven trays, and regional specialties. Visitors can sample dishes such as Mi Quang,pork rice paper rolls served with fermented anchovy sauce, and sticky rice cake wrapped in leaves. The cultural program also includes performances featuring the dan tranh , a traditional Vietnamese zither, and bamboo flutes, alongside activities such as making two figurines and painting conical hats. A "Viet Gifts" area introduces handicrafts and souvenirs inspired by Vietnamese traditional craft villages, giving visitors additional opportunities to explore local culture. Photos courtesy of Sun Group

picked.t: Death toll from Hanoi eatery blast rises to 7
picked.body: The latest victim was a 24-year-old woman who succumbed to multiple injuries at Saint Paul Hospital, a representative from Hanoi's Health Department said Tuesday night. Another victim died at Dong Da General Hospital. His body, covered with a blanket, was taken away from the hospital in an ambulance. Preliminary reports indicated that he was walking past the eatery when the blast tore off his clothes and flying debris injured him. Hanoi police said a suspected gas blast partially collapsed a single-story building behind the E4 apartment block on Nguyen Van Tuyet Street in Dong Da Ward. Investigators are still working to determine what triggered the blast. The explosion shook a three-story apartment block behind the eatery, neighboring buildings and a row of houses across Nguyen Van Tuyet Street. It cracked walls, shattered windows and brought down corrugated metal roofs and awnings. Authorities are assessing the damage and have relocated residents from buildings deemed structurally unsafe. The eatery was packed when the blast struck, raising fears that more people may be trapped under the debris. Police are using detection equipment to search for survivors and hydraulic machinery to lift concrete slabs. The blast occurred at around 8 a.m. near a gas stove as the eatery at 168 Nguyen Van Tuyet Street was opening for business. It shook the ground and damaged about 10 houses within 15 meters, tearing roll-up doors from their frames and causing roofs to collapse. Debris covered more than 20 meters of the street, and several motorcycles were knocked over. Police and residents searched the rubble for victims, and local residents carried several injured people out and took them to hospital for emergency treatment. Ly Ngoc Chung, who lives about 100 meters away, said the explosion woke him and shook his house violently. He rushed outside and, on reaching the scene, saw damaged homes and injured people lying among the debris.
